tools.name: search_hotels
tools.description: Use this when the user wants hotels in a destination (e.g. 'quiet hotels in Bangkok under $150'), or asks about a hotel by name (hotel_name). tools.name: get_hotel
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one hotel: why it scores as it does, or whether it's quiet, clean or good for sleep or work. Returns the Comfort Score breakdown, what the scores rest on, the five must-haves, its strengths and complaints with the reason behind each score, price, the city tax where

tools.name: list_cities
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which destinations OKstays covers, or before planning a trip through a country. Returns every destination we score with its country, slug and number of hotels; pass country to list one country only. Read-only, no sign-in.

tools.name: get_filters
tools.description: Use this to look up the comfort signals and travel styles that search_hotels accepts, when the user's wish doesn't map clearly to one. Returns every filter (id, name, description, category, whether it's a must-have) and every travel style. Plain names also work in search_hotels tags ('quiet', 'wifi'

tools.name: compare_hotels
tools.description: Use this when the user is choosing between 2-4 specific hotels. Returns each hotel's Comfort Score breakdown, price, strengths and complaints, the signals where they differ most, and a verdict: best comfort, cheapest, best value. tools.name: find_similar_hotels
tools.description: Use this when the user likes a hotel but wants alternatives, e.g. 'like this one but cheaper' (cheaper_only).
